items.title: DeepSeek V4 Pro beats GPT-5.5 Pro on precision
items.author: yogthos
items.summary: DeepSeek V4 Pro outperforms GPT-5.5 Pro in precision and coding benchmarks while costing significantly less. It offers near-frontier performance at a fraction of the price. DeepSeek V4 redefines value with aggressive pricing and accessibility.

items.title: The Smallest Brain You Can Build: A Perceptron in Python
items.author: DevarshRanpara
items.summary: A perceptron is a simple neural network model. It uses a learning rule to adjust weights based on input and output. The smallest perceptron can be implemented in Python with a few lines of code.

items.title: 1worldflag: A blue dot on a transparent background
items.author: davidbarker
items.summary: The One World Flag features a blue dot representing Earth on a transparent background, symbolizing our shared planet. Designed by Thomas Mandl in 2016, it has gained viral attention for its minimalist design. The flag's transparent background adapts to its surroundings.

items.title: Texas grid flags risks as data centers, crypto sites fail voltage tests
items.author: 1vuio0pswjnm7
items.summary: Texas grid warns of risks as data centers and crypto sites fail voltage tests, potentially causing power outages during peak demand. The rapid expansion of data centers is straining the grid. This issue highlights the need for better grid infrastructure.

items.title: 7.8 magnitude earthquake shakes part of southern Philippines. Tsunami possible
items.author: mikhael
items.summary: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck the southern Philippines, triggering a tsunami warning and causing power outages; no immediate damage reports are available. The quake's epicenter was near General Santos city on Mindanao. Tsunami waves up to 10 feet were possible in the Philippines.

items.title: Powering up a module from the IBM 604: an electronic calculator from 1948
items.author: elpocko
items.summary: To power up the IBM 604, connect it to a power source, plug in the Type 521 Card Reader/Punch, and set the plugboard for desired calculations. The 604 performs operations based on its wiring and outputs results on punched cards.

items.title: Show HN: Lathe – Use LLMs to learn a new domain, not skip past it
items.author: devenjarvis
items.text:
Hey HN!

Lathe is an experiment in using LLMs to teach me something new, instead of doing the work for me. It generates a hands-on, source-backed tutorial for any technical topic you want to learn. Then you work through it yourself by reading and typing the code by hand (gasp) in a local UI built for exactly that.

It's a Go CLI plus LLM agent skills (Claude Code / Cursor / Codex). You prompt something like "/lathe build a 3D slicer in Erlang", run `lathe s
items.summary: Lathe uses LLMs to guide self-learning in new domains through interactive tutorials. It emphasizes hands-on coding and critical thinking. It features a local UI with exercises and verified content.

items.title: LLMs are eroding my software engineering career and I don't know what to do
items.author: poisonfountain
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) may reduce demand for certain coding tasks, but expertise in code quality and software architecture remains crucial. Focus on these areas to maintain employability. The job market still values ML and AI engineers.

items.title: Man-Computer Symbiosis J. C. R. Licklider (1960)
items.author: rballpug
items.summary: J. C. R. Licklider's 1960 work "Man-Computer Symbiosis" envisioned a close partnership between humans and computers to enhance capabilities. This concept evolved into human-AI symbiosis, reflecting ongoing advancements in AI and collaboration.

items.title: KNN early termination in Manticore Search
items.author: snikolaev
items.summary: KNN early termination in Manticore Search reduces unnecessary distance computations by stopping search early when results converge. It significantly cuts distance calculations, especially for larger k values. This optimization improves search efficiency.

items.title: An Ohio Valley 100k-watt FM signal is severed in broad daylight
items.author: pkaeding
items.summary: A 100,000-watt FM signal in Ohio Valley was cut by Paul Crisp, disrupting WDGG(FM) broadcasting. Crisp allegedly stole and cut the transmission line for copper. The incident caused significant disruption to the station's signal.

items.title: Office-open-xml-viewer: Office XML document viewer that renders to HTML Canvas
items.author: maxloh
items.summary: Silurus/ooxml renders Office documents to HTML Canvas. Another viewer is OpenXmlFileViewer for editing XML components. Wikipedia lists software supporting Office Open XML.

items.title: Anthropic, please ship an official Claude Desktop for Linux
items.author: predkambrij
items.summary: Anthropic does not officially offer a Claude Desktop app for Linux; only macOS and Windows are supported. The official option is the Claude Code CLI for Linux. Community projects provide unofficial desktop builds.

items.title: I design with Claude more than Figma now
items.author: MrBuddyCasino
items.summary: Designers increasingly favor Claude over Figma for iterative design tasks due to its flexibility and speed. Many find it easier to refine designs quickly with minimal hassle. Some still use Figma for collaborative projects.

items.title: Jeff Bezos Is Funding a Wild Hunt for the Brain's 'Core Algorithm'
items.author: uxhacker
items.summary: Jeff Bezos funds Flourish, a neuro AI company aiming to reinvent AI by studying real neurons, with $500 million in funding and a $2.5 billion valuation. Flourish focuses on cortical columns, believed to be the brain's computational units.

items.title: Tokenomics: Quantifying Where Tokens Are Used in Agentic Software Engineering
items.author: Anon84
items.summary: Tokenomics studies token usage in LLM-based multi-agent systems for software engineering. The research focuses on token consumption patterns across development stages. The study uses ChatDev and GPT-5 as its models.

items.title: Ask HN: What was your "oh shit" moment with GenAI?
items.author: andrehacker
items.text:
Most of us were amused when DALL-E and its peers went mainstream, and we were quick to point out the obvious flaws.

Then ChatGPT hit the scene and again, many of us dismissed it as a parlor trick that would never amount to much.

Using LLMs for coding initially was a only small step up from basic code completion, and a welcome farewell to Stack Overflow.

I am curious: what was the specific moment that you went from those quaint, dismissive observations to a slightly panicked, "Uh Oh&qu
items.summary: My "oh shit" moment with GenAI was realizing its potential to automate complex tasks. It highlighted the need for ethical guidelines. GenAI's capabilities are impressive but require careful oversight.
